correctness.rationale: The asymmetric payoff difference in Jiang's Appendix C reduces to the frozen equations at N=2. For D=δ_s+δ_d, q(p)=δ_s−Dp, a=r/2−1, use the physical-time coordinates u=log(x/(1−x))−1/x and v=log(p/(1−p)). Each is an increasing diffeomorphism onto R. The transformed system satisfies u̇=a/x+(r/2)q(p), v̇=ε[(1+θ)x−1], and its divergence in (u,v) is −a(1−x), of strict sign off r=2. Thus Bendixson–Dulac excludes every nonconstant periodic interior orbit there, irrespective of equilibrium existence. At r=2 the separated Hamiltonian in (u,v) has derivatives H_u=ε[(1+θ)x(u)−1], H_v=Dp(v)−δ_s, with u̇=−H_v and v̇=H_u. Each derivative strictly increases and tends to nonzero limits of opposite signs, so H is strictly convex, proper and has a unique minimum at the stated coexistence point. Its other levels are smooth compact circles with a nowhere vanishing tangent flow, hence form a family of periodic orbits. Integrating v̇, u̇, and d log(x/(1−x))/dt=xq(p) over each full period gives respectively the stated mean x, mean p, and mean xp; these are physical-time identities and give zero covariance. The PDF version inspected numbers the general model Eq. (7) and gives the asymmetric formula in Appendix C; the frozen Eq. (11) locator was not confirmed in that version, but the stated vector field is correct.
